decisions.difference: A: (New medication commenced finding)  vs  B: (Exposure to (contextual qualifier) + Drug or medicament)
decisions.reason: "started any medication ... in the past 3 months" needs an exposure with an onset; B's exposure form is the gold standard's pattern, while the onset of a 'New medication commenced' finding is a roundabout reading.

decisions.difference: A: (none)  vs  B: (Infestation caused by Ixodidae), (Infestation caused by Argasidae)
decisions.final_expr: (finding (snomed_concept "Clinical finding" "finding") (snomed_concept "Infestation caused by Ixodidae" "disorder")); (finding ... "Infestation caused by Argasidae" ...)
decisions.reason: The page says "If tick bite or tick present"; A dropped "tick present" entirely, B covers it with the hard- and soft-tick infestation concepts.

decisions.difference: A: (none)  vs  B: lesion of genitalia / anus / rectum / mouth / eye
decisions.final_expr: (Lesion of genitalia), (Lesion + finding_site Anal structure), (Lesion of rectum), (Oral lesion), (Lesion of eye)
decisions.reason: The page lists "lesion/s of skin/genitals/anus/rectum/mouth/eyes" as mpox evidence and both builds use them in the mpox rule, so the task asks for them; A omitted them only because the rash already satisfies that part (raised as a clinician question).

decisions.difference: A: onset of New medication commenced <= 3 months  vs  B: onset of exposure to Drug or medicament <= 3 months
decisions.final_expr: (<= (onset (finding (snomed_concept "Exposure to (contextual qualifier)" "qualifier value") (snomed_concept "Drug or medicament" "substance"))) (time_ago 3 months))
decisions.reason: Same as the check_for decision: "started any medication" in the past 3 months is the onset of a drug exposure, and the examples are "such as" so the generic substance fits.

decisions.difference: A: (none)  vs  B: Infestation caused by Ixodidae / Argasidae in the tick-bite-fever rule
decisions.final_expr: (or Tick bite, Infestation caused by Ixodidae, Infestation caused by Argasidae)
decisions.reason: "If tick bite or tick present" is a disjunction; B encodes both halves.

decisions.difference: A: Generalized rash required in the tick-bite-fever rule  vs  B: not required
decisions.reason: The bullet sits on the GENERALISED NON-ITCHY RASH page and every other diagnosis rule in both builds requires the rash as page context; without it the rule would diagnose tick bite fever on any page's patient.

decisions.difference: A: Generalized rash listed in the mpox 'rash or lesion' or  vs  B: Skin lesion only
decisions.reason: "rash or lesion/s of skin": snomed is_a confirms Generalized rash is a descendant of Skin lesion, so A's extra disjunct is redundant and B's form matches the page's wording.

decisions.difference: A: African tick bite fever (probable)  vs  B: Spotted fever group rickettsial disease (probable)
decisions.reason: The page says only "tick bite fever", which covers both African tick bite fever and Boutonneuse fever (both children of the spotted-fever parent); A's choice is narrower than the page, but the page does not name an organism.

notes: Both builds passed. Base is B (it encodes 'tick present' and the lesion sites; A omitted them). One change from A: the tick-bite-fever rule now also requires the generalised rash, consistent with the other five rules. Rule descriptions keep B's '(generalised rash page)' wording. Remaining questions merged from both builds; A's questions on syphilis-titer recording, HIV-positive diagnosis and the No-branch reading were kept, and a question about asking lesion sites was added.
